text: The central ledger is written only by the ingest of rwb.decision-record.v1; no REST append operation is declared for rwb-decision.
why: The Ownership Map gives P7 the two GET paths only, and Architecture v5 slide 14 lists no ledger POST; the consumer of the shared topic is the only writer described by the design.
read: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rows (GET /decision-log, GET /decision-log/{entryId}); Architecture v5 slide 14 IN/OUT for rwb-decision; slide 28 ingest design.
confirm: The rwb-decision service owner confirms that no caller writes the ledger over REST in wave 1 and that a sibling P7 story declaring POST /decision-log is corrected.
impact: If a write path is needed, a story and an Ownership Map row must be added before wave 1 build; nothing else in this key changes.

text: The central chain is built by recomputing entry_hash on the legacy canonical form (BR4) over the stored columns, appending under one advisory lock in ingest commit order, and keeping the local chain sequence and hash on the row for reconciliation.
why: The legacy algorithm is fixed but its application to nineteen independent local chains is not; one deterministic rule is needed for AC2, AC4 and AC5 to be testable.
read: RWB-E1-008 BR3 and BR4; Temporal and Drools design slide 16; Architecture v5 slide 28.
confirm: The solution architect signs the rule off before the golden hash vectors of the ledger are frozen.
impact: A different rule changes the entry_hash values and the verifier's expected results, not the table or the API.

text: The data-lake copy of the decision log is retired; JOB-13 is the continuous ingest, JOB-14 is the 02:00 chain check with a daily WORM seal, and FEAT-DRI-06 has no target.
why: Architecture v5 removes the lake (DP-17, ADR-018) and reuses JOB-13 for the continuous ingest, while the FSD module still describes the copy.
read: Architecture v5 slides 37 and 44; Template and Rules §R6; FSD P7 A2.6.
confirm: The business analyst of P7 withdraws FEAT-DRI-06 in the next FSD version.
impact: No lake object, partition, manifest or watermark is built; reporting reads events, so no report loses a source.

text: A strict-mode waiter confirms its record by reading GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId} until the sealed entry is returned, and the sealed entry is also announced on rwb.decision-record.v1 for the reporting projection.
why: The design requires a confirmation before a point of no return but names no mechanism; the read is the one contract that already exists and needs no new operation.
read: Architecture v5 slide 28 (strict decision-log mode); Temporal and Drools design (points of no return); Ownership Map decision-log reads.
confirm: The solution architect and the integration lead confirm the mechanism in the wave 1 integration harness before a strict-mode step goes live.
impact: A signal-based confirmation would add one activity and one contract element; the read needs nothing further.

text: The three library objects are created in rwb_decision by RWB-P7-E1008-DB under the X row, and the ingest is built against the published template of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON without a build dependency on it.
why: DP-09 is not in the story's patterns and RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is not in its H row, while the consumer still needs the inbox object and the announcement needs the outbox object.
read: Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20; Ownership Map rows outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key.
confirm: The platform event owner confirms the template version and that no build dependency is needed to consume the topic.
impact: If the H row is corrected, nothing in the story changes except the metadata row and the dependency graph.

text: The page read defaults to page 1 and size 50, accepts a size up to 200, and answers an RFC 9457 problem body with type, title, status, detail and the message identifier.
why: The legacy contract names page and size and four errors without values or a body, and the contract story cannot be tested without them.
read: RWB-E1-008 section 12; API Specification v4 decision-log entries.
confirm: The contract owner of rwb-decision confirms the values with the query-API story RWB-P7-E2005-CON before v1 is frozen.
impact: A different default or maximum is a documentation and test change and not a schema change.

text: The published ledger read path is /decision-log under /api/recovery/decision/v1, as the Ownership Map and the legacy story name it, and the /decisions path of Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 is corrected in the next architecture version.
why: Two sources disagree; Template and Rules §R3 puts the catalogue slides above the narrative, but the Ownership Map row cites the API Specification and the legacy path, and the two catalogue statements are themselves inconsistent.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rows; RWB-E1-008 section 12.
confirm: The solution architect confirms the correction of the two slides at the next architecture review.
impact: No code change; one path is published and every consumer uses it.

text: decision_log_entry.case_id is a plain uuid with no foreign key; the case is verified through the P3 case contract on the read, and corrects_entry_id keeps its self-reference at the application level.
why: The legacy key crosses into recovery_case, which in the target is another service's schema, and DP-01 forbids a cross-schema key.
read: Physical Schema v6 DDL; TSD P7 T3.3; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 29.
confirm: The ACE data architect confirms the ruling for every legacy cross-module key of the decision log.
impact: An entry may name a case that no longer exists; the read answers 404 with MSG-P4-003 and the ledger keeps the row as it was written.

text: The service login is created by the platform DB work as rwb-decision under the platform naming convention, the schema owner is a separate role used only by migrations, and the three library objects are applied from the published event platform template unchanged.
why: AC1 depends on a login without UPDATE and DELETE and an owner that the trigger refuses, and the story may not invent a credential or a column set.
read: RWB-E1-008 AC1 and section 3; Ownership Map rows for the three PLT objects; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 20.
confirm: The platform DB owner confirms the naming convention and the owner separation at the DB review.
impact: A different login name is a grant-script and chart change only.

text: The ingest uses consumer group rwb-decision-ledger, alerts at 5 minutes of lag and on the first dead letter, runs the append-only verification one hour before the 02:00 chain check, and writes the seal to a per-environment immutable-storage path.
why: The deployment needs concrete values for its alerts, its job and its seal target, and no source fixes them.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14, 28 and 44; Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3.
confirm: The DevOps lead and the platform observability owner confirm the thresholds and the seal path per environment.
impact: Thresholds and the job time are configuration; a different group name rewinds the offsets once.

text: A restore of the ledger targets a point in time after the last verified seal and is promoted only after the chain is re-verified end to end and the append-only verification passes; no statement is run on a ledger row to make a check pass.
why: The ledger may not be repaired, so the only safe recovery is a restore proved by the chain and the seals.
read: REQ-DRI-002 and REQ-DRI-003; DL26; Architecture v5 slide 14 (daily ledger seal in immutable storage).
confirm: The DevOps lead and the resilience owner set the RPO and RTO and run one restore exercise per release.
impact: A restore that cannot reach the last seal loses the entries after it and must be reported to Compliance as a break.

text: The write surface of the decision log writer is the local decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON plus the service-local append of RWB-P7-E1008-APP, called in process on task queue rwb-decision, and no REST write operation is declared.
why: The Ownership Map gives P7 only two read operations and the target writes the record inside the caller's transaction, so a REST append would be an invented operation.
read: _work/msr/plan/ownership.json api rows GET /decision-log and GET /decision-log/{entryId}; Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 28; DP-03 and DP-11
confirm: Solution architect confirms the local operation with the Ownership Map owner and records it, or asks for one owned command path.
impact: If a command path is required, section 12.1 of both stories and the fakes gain one operation; no behaviour of the writer changes.

text: The record carries the legacy field groups DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-030 and DF-DEC-031, the chain columns of the design, a data date and an inputs reference with a digest; the column widths, the data-date column name, the digest algorithm, the local retention and the catalogue entry format are used as the working read.
why: The field groups and identifiers are specified but the physical form is not, and the story cannot be built or tested without one fixed shape.
read: RWB-E1-027 sections 11, 12 and 14; LDM v8 DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031; Temporal and Drools Design slide 16
confirm: Data steward and the Physical Schema owner fix the column list in rwb_decision.sql and in the contract baseline.
impact: A changed column list changes section 11 and 12.7 of both stories and the fixtures of the fakes; no criterion changes.

text: The entry hash is SHA-256 over a canonical form that fixes the field order of the record, UTF-8 encoding, no insignificant whitespace, a null rendered as an empty string and a 64-character lowercase hexadecimal digest, with 64 zeros as the first previous hash.
why: The digest algorithm and the first link are specified, the canonicalisation is not, and the chain check of the store story needs one reproducible input.
read: FSD P7 A2.1 AC-ALT-P7-001-01; Temporal and Drools Design slide 16
confirm: Solution architect and the store owner publish one cross-language fixture and adopt it in RWB-P7-E1008-APP.
impact: A different canonical form changes the chain fixture and every stored digest; the criteria keep their wording and the values change.

text: DecisionRecorded is published as rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, and the platform library contract is to be corrected from rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1.
why: Two contract documents of this run publish two types for one shared topic, and one type is required before the registry subject can be created.
read: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON 12.3; RWB-P6-E1052-CON AC6 and 12.3; Architecture v5 slide 42 event 08
confirm: Solution architect adopts one type and the platform library contract is corrected in its next version.
impact: If the platform type wins, section 12.3 of both stories, the envelope fake and the registry subject change together.

text: The decision log writes no data-lake copy: the legacy stream and its 01:00 job are retired and reporting reads the events through rwb-reporting.
why: Architecture v5 removes the data lake and DP-17 retires RWB-E1-014, so keeping the stream would contradict the higher source.
read: Architecture v5 slides 37 and 41; DP-17; Template and Rules §R6 Retired row RWB-E1-014
confirm: Business analyst removes A2.6 from the next version of the P7 module specification.
impact: No lake sink, no watermark and no retention step; the reporting need moves to the event projection.

text: The ledger ingest is continuous from rwb.decision-record.v1 in RWB-P7-E1008-APP, JOB-14 at 02:00 stays the only Schedule of this service, and the writer declares no Schedule and reads no shared Quartz table.
why: The architecture makes the ingest continuous and retires the shared Quartz tables, while the module specification still describes a nightly copy job.
read: Architecture v5 slide 44 JOB-13 and JOB-14; DP-10; Template and Rules §R6 Retired row RWB-TE-007
confirm: Solution architect confirms the ingest model and the retirement of JOB-13 in the Batch and Scheduling next version.
impact: 12.6 reads None in both stories, and a Schedule appears only in the store story.

text: decision_log_entry keeps every entry with no purge, no archive and no truncation in this story, and the retention period is read as a parameter when Compliance publishes it.
why: NFR-030 leaves the period open under DL26 and DP-17 removes the lake copy, so no value can be written and no deletion can be designed.
read: NFR-030; Decision Log v10 DL26; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 28; FSD P7 A2.1
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, with the P7 business lead
impact: If the period arrives as a class shorter than the ledger's life, one Schedule and one reference row are added; the two reads and the export do not change.

text: The export is the same GET with Accept text/csv, streamed page by page by the service, and the 2 s budget applies to each page of 500 rows rather than to the whole population.
why: The legacy flow returns the full result as CSV while the target fixes one hop and a 2 s timeout, and no source fixes an export size, a column order or a file hand-off.
read: RWB-E2-005 section 4 step 7, section 12 and AC8; Architecture v5 slide 11; ADR-020
confirm: Solution architect, with the TechX lead of rwb-decision
impact: If the architect rules for an asynchronous file through rwb-integration instead, one consumption is added and the AC-EXPT record names the file reference; the query path is unchanged.

text: The audit read returns the masked value of the free-text fields under the policy of rwb-access in force, offers no unmasking operation, and the export carries the same masking as the screen.
why: The legacy guardrail masks before export and gives no audit exception, and the target gives no unmasking right to RW-AUDIT.
read: RWB-E2-005 AC8 and section 17; NFR-039 and NFR-040; Ownership Map row masking_rule owner P4
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer
impact: If an audit-specific policy row is published, one policy read changes and no field of the answer changes.

text: REQ-ACA-006 and NFR-042 are read as covering the case store, the document store and the reporting read model, and the legacy lake analysis is retired with no target path.
why: Architecture v5 removes the data lake and the preservation rule retires RWB-E1-014, so the wording of the two requirements names a sink that no longer exists.
read: REQ-ACA-006; NFR-042; Architecture v5 slide 37; Template and Rules §R6
confirm: Business analyst, P7, with Compliance
impact: The query path logs no lake read and holds no lake dependency; the next BRD and NFR version reword the two requirements.

text: The authorise answer of rwb-access carries the scope kind and the case-scope predicate, the service applies it to the case ID of each entry, the case facts of the scope test come from the P3 case read in the contract dependencies, and the chain-mismatch incident goes to the Compliance queue read from platform configuration.
why: The legacy story filters scope through two published interfaces and names no Ownership Map operation for either, and no source names the incident queue.
read: RWB-E2-005 sections 4, 10 and 12; Architecture v5 slide 13 notes; RWB-P4-E1037-CON; RWB-P3-E2041-CON
confirm: Solution architect, with the P4 access owner and the P3 case owner
impact: If P4 answers the owned case keys instead of a predicate, the filter compares a set and the query plan changes; if the queue is named, one configuration row changes.

text: RWB-P7-E1008-APP owns the table baseline, its keys and its append-only trigger, and this story adds one index-only migration for (approver_user_id, decided_at) in the same per-service sequence after that baseline.
why: The legacy story adds the index to a table that another story of the same key now creates, and no source fixes which story owns a later index on an earlier story's table.
read: RWB-E2-005 section 13; DP-15; plan slice RWB-P7-E1008-APP
confirm: ACE team, with the TechX lead of rwb-decision
impact: If the baseline story takes the index, the migration of this story is dropped and AC4 keeps its target; no read changes.

text: The first page of a query over 10,000 matching entries answers inside 3 seconds, and the number is a parameter rather than a constant.
why: The legacy story states the measure as assumed under DL11 and no non-functional requirement fixes a number.
read: RWB-E2-005 section 2; TSD P7 v2 Appendix T-B DL11; NFR-036
confirm: Solution architect, with the QA lead
impact: If DL11 rules a different target, one parameter row changes and the performance case is re-baselined; no read or field changes.

text: The page carries messageCodes and the entry carries chainVerified and the eleven audit elements, and the remaining element names, the CSV column order and the page-size default are published as the working read.
why: The legacy contract and the TSD name the two components without a schema, so the element list beyond the legacy names has no source.
read: RWB-E2-005 section 12; TSD P7 v2 T-A.2; RWB-P7-E1008-APP canonical form
confirm: Solution architect, with the TechX lead of rwb-decision
impact: A confirmed name is a rename inside major version 1 before v1 freezes; after the freeze it is a new major version.

text: The 401 answer carries the platform identifier MSG-P4-001 of the authorise contract, and the contract test asserts the status until the platform catalogue binds it.
why: The legacy contract lists 401 without an identifier and no message catalogue read here binds one to the audit read.
read: RWB-E2-005 section 12; RWB-P4-E1037-CON message rows
confirm: Platform library owner
impact: One mapping row of section 14 changes; no status and no shape changes.

text: The AC-READ and AC-EXPT record is written locally through the decision-record library at the P7 router and relayed on rwb.decision-record.v1, and the access log of rwb-access reads it back rather than writing it.
why: The legacy story writes the access events through RWB-E1-039 while the target gives the local decision record to each service and the access log to P4, and no source says which carries these two codes.
read: RWB-E2-005 sections 4, 11 and 17; DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON AC2; RWB-P4-E1039-CON
confirm: Solution architect, with the P4 access owner
impact: If P4 must own the write, one consumption is added and the AC-DENY, AC-READ and AC-EXPT codes move to the P4 access log; the two reads of this story do not change.

text: The delegation of authority table, its versions, its holders and its substitutes stay in rwb-access and are read on GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits; rwb-decision applies the routing rule over that answer and stores delegationLimitId, approvalLevel and limitVersion on the approval, with no join, view or foreign key across the two schemas.
why: The target gives the table and the authorise decision to P4 and the approval, the routing and the decision record to P7, and the legacy story already reads the holders through the P4 interface, so the rule can live in P7 while the data stays with its owner.
read: Ownership Map v1 (delegation_limit owner P4 and ruling); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and T3.3; legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 4, 8, 11 and 12.
applied_in: RWB-P7-E2013-APP sections 2, 8 BR13, 11, 12.2 and 12.7; RWB-P7-E2013-CON AC4 and 12.7
confirm: Solution architect with the P4 and P7 owners in the RWB-P7-E2013-CON baseline review.
impact: If the routing rule moves to P4, one P4 operation is added and routeApproval becomes a call; no schema, event or table change here.

text: GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits is the delegation read of P4 rwb-access, with the decision, the regulation item, the product, the amounts and the on-date as the query and the delegation row reference, level, holder, substitute, version and effective date as the answer; the app story and the contract fakes build against that path and the RWB-P4-E1037-CON document fixes it.
why: Two architecture slides name GET /doa-limits and the Ownership Map simply has no row for it, so the path has to be named from the architecture and the contract rather than from a catalogue entry that does not exist.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Ownership Map v1 api section; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 appendix T-A.
applied_in: RWB-P7-E2013-APP sections 3, 12.2, 12.8 and AC4; RWB-P7-E2013-CON section 12.2 and AC4; RWB-P7-E2013-OPS AC6
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access owner before the wave 2 SIT entry.
impact: If P4 publishes another path or a batch load instead, one consumed row, one client adapter and one fake change; no schema or event change.

text: The service level and the escalation run on three data values: rwb.approval.route.<decision>.service-level and rwb.approval.service-level.default as the legacy assumes them (1 working day for D7.1, 3 working days default, DL22), one working day per escalation step as AC2 shows, and rwb.approval.escalation.max-levels with the behaviour at the ceiling held as data with no value until the register closes the point.
why: The legacy story marks both service level values as assumed and gives no ceiling, while the capability cannot be built or deployed without one step length and one ceiling rule.
read: legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 3, 4 step 9, AC2 and AC3; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-30 and R-UNI-42.
applied_in: RWB-P7-E2013-APP sections 3, 4, 13 configuration; RWB-P7-E2013-OPS sections 11 and 13
confirm: Business lead with the Center of excellence at the RWB-P7-E2013-CON baseline review.
impact: A different step length or ceiling changes one parameter row and one test; no schema, event or workflow change.

text: The approval outcome reaches reporting only through rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 and the projections of rwb-reporting; no lake partition, manifest, watermark or daily copy exists for this capability, and INT-19 and INT-20 are retired with the lake.
why: DP-17 removes the data lake and RWB-E1-014 is retired, while the module specification still lists two daily lake batches and a lake stream of the decision log.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 28, 37 and 44; plan DP-17; TSD P7 v2 T5.1; FSD P7 A2.6; Template and Rules R6.
applied_in: RWB-P7-E2013-APP sections 12.3 and 19; RWB-P7-E2013-CON section 12.3 and 19
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-reporting owner.
impact: No change to the approval or its events; one lake row and one batch story disappear from the module specification.

text: The five approval resources are baselined from the TSD P7 T3.1 field names in camelCase plus the platform page and error conventions: ApprovalAction carries reason, resolutionReference, reasonCode, changes and membersPresent; ApprovalDetail adds the routing detail; ApprovalPage carries the page metadata with a default and a maximum size; and the case-status move is one operation or one subscription named in RWB-P7-E2013-CON, not an open query.
why: T-A.2 names the resources and no property list, the legacy gives business names only, and the case status the flow names has no operation in the Ownership Map, so the baseline has to fix all four before the build.
read: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and appendix T-A.2; legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 4 and 12; Ownership Map v1 api section; FSD P7 A2.15 to A2.25.
applied_in: RWB-P7-E2013-APP section 12.1 and 12.2; RWB-P7-E2013-CON AC1, AC2, AC5 and AC8; RWB-P7-E2013-OPS section 11
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-decision with the Solution architect at the baseline review.
impact: Settling a property list or the page size changes the contract test and the fakes only; the case-status decision may add one consumed row or one consumed event.

text: The delegation snapshot is a local read-through cache of the version in force, warmed before the readiness probe passes and refreshed on rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 by its effective date; the service copies no table, an open approval keeps the version already stamped on it, and an alert fires when the cached version is older than the version in force.
why: The routing must use the version in force and the open item must keep its own version, while no source names a store, an interval or an owner for the refresh.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41 and 42; Ownership Map v1 (delegation_limit owner P4); legacy RWB-E2-013 sections 3, 4 step 10 and AC3.
applied_in: RWB-P7-E2013-APP section 4 step 10 and 12.4; RWB-P7-E2013-OPS AC6, section 15 and 13
confirm: Solution architect with the platform observability owner and the rwb-access owner.
impact: A different refresh rule changes one deployment step, one fake and one alert; no schema or event change.

text: No P7 story of this key publishes ApprovalDecided: the approval outcome leaves as DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 and the request leaves as ApprovalRequested on rwb.decision.events.v1, and ApprovalDecided is carried as an absence in the baseline until the catalogue gives it a row, a number and its consumers.
why: The service contract slide names an event the catalogue does not carry, and the legacy story and the module specification publish only ApprovalRequested and DecisionRecorded.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 42; TSD P7 v2 T5.3; legacy RWB-E2-013 section 12.
confirm: Solution architect with the event platform owner.
impact: If ApprovalDecided is catalogued, one published event, one consumer contract and one test are added; no schema change.

text: The field list and the mask flags of the two panels are published in RWB-P7-E2014-CON as the working read: approvalId, caseId, caseNo, decisionCode, approvalStatus, routeRoleCode, dueAt, escalationLevel, preparedBy, productGroup, ruleId, ruleVersion, noticeId, noticeType, noticeState, templateId, templateVersion, documentId, inputFacts and postalAddress, with inputFacts as a list of inputCode, businessDate, ageDays, limitDays and stale.
why: The legacy story fixes the facts on the screen but no source enumerates the model or its flags, and the app story cannot build a screen without a field list.
read: RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 4, AC10 and section 15 read together with RWB-PLT-N001-CON 12.1 and the FSD P7 Screens table.
confirm: Route owner and the three consumer sign-offs of RWB-P7-E2014-CON
impact: A field added or renamed later is a new contract version and a new screen build step; no business value depends on the list.

text: The screen is served at the public route GET /api/recovery/approvals/{approvalId} on the gateway-bff public base /api/recovery, with no service segment and no /v1.
why: The legacy story names the screen only by SCR-11 and SCR-18 and the platform contract publishes seven other routes, so a name has to be chosen to build and register the screen.
read: RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC1 and 12.1 (public base and the seven published routes) with RWB-E2-014 section 4 (the owner operations the screen reads).
confirm: Platform route owner at the first contract version freeze
impact: If the route owner chooses another segment, the contract, the app story and the smoke job change and no business value does.

text: For D7.1 the limit that applies on the screen is read as no amount limit at approval level none, shown as the approval level and the route role, and the DoA table is not consulted for this decision; the DoA table stays P4 rwb-access' and is read by the routing story where an amount-bearing decision uses it.
why: REQ-APD-002 asks for the limit on the screen while the legacy story states that a D7.1 notice carries none, and the two readings must be reconciled in one place.
read: RWB-E2-014 section 10 row 'Approval level | None'; REQ-APD-002; Architecture v5 slide 14 (P7 reads DoA limits) and slide 41 (P4 owns the DoA table).
confirm: Business lead with Risk and Credit
impact: If a limit must be shown, one field and one P4 read are added; no approval outcome of D7.1 changes.

text: No data-lake element exists in this key: INT-19, INT-20 and the daily decision-log copy are retired, the record is published on rwb.decision-record.v1 and reporting reads events, and JOB-13 is continuous Kafka ingest in the owning service.
why: The module specification keeps two daily lake interfaces and a daily copy while DP-17 and ADR-018 remove the lake, and the stories and the deployment must choose one reading.
read: Architecture v5 slides 37 and 44 (JOB-13) with DP-17, ADR-018 and TSD P7 v2 T5.1.
confirm: Data steward and data product owner in the next module-specification version
impact: Documentation only; no story, chart or run book carries a lake element.

text: The decided outcome of a D7.1 approval is published only as rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 through the local decision-record library; no ApprovalDecided envelope is published by this key.
why: The slide 14 contract line names ApprovalDecided and the event catalogue of slides 42 and 43 does not, so one of the two has to be followed.
read: Architecture v5 slide 14 against slide 42 row 09, slide 43 row 30 and DP-03.
confirm: Solution architect in the next event-catalogue version
impact: A consumer that expected ApprovalDecided reads the decision record instead; rwb-reporting already consumes it.

text: REQ-APD-002 and REQ-APD-006 are traced to FEAT-APD-08 with RWB-E2-014 for the screen and to FEAT-APD-01 with RWB-E2-013 for the routing, as the FSD declares them.
why: The FSD and the TSD traceability table map the same two requirements to two different features and stories.
read: FSD P7 v3 A1.2 and A2.22 against TSD P7 v2 T8.
confirm: Business analyst in the next TSD version
impact: Traceability reporting only; both stories remain in the same wave.

text: The three notice operations the legacy story calls are consumed as the notice decision operations of the rwb-comms contract, addressed on the notice: approve, regenerate from another Approved variant and hold with a reason code; they are built and faked until the owner publishes them.
why: AC1, AC2 and AC3 cannot pass without a path for the three calls and the Ownership Map names none.
read: RWB-E2-014 section 12 published interface NoticeApi with RWB-P6-E1052-CON 12.1 and the Ownership Map api rows for rwb-comms.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-comms owner
impact: If the owner publishes one decision operation instead, the adapter and three contract-test rows change and no criterion changes.

text: The total balance and the masked postal address are read through the rwb-source-data data-product contract with data_as_of, and the case number and the case-owner task through the rwb-case contract, with no v_ace_* read of rwb-decision; both are consumed against their fakes and one C row each is added when the register closes.
why: The screen needs two owners' facts and this key's contract dependency list carries neither, while only rwb-source-data may read the ACE views.
read: Architecture v5 slide 45 (ADR-010) with RWB-E2-014 section 11 and the contract dependency list of this story.
confirm: Solution architect at the dependency-map sign-off
impact: Two C rows and two contract-test rows are added; the build is not blocked because both are faked from Day 1.

text: The page size of the queue read defaults to 20 with a maximum of 100, and the field types and order of the screen model are as RWB-P7-E2014-CON declares them.
why: The module specification names the four query parameters but no default, maximum or page shape, and the model's types are stated nowhere.
read: TSD P7 v2 T-A.2 API-P7-002 with RWB-E2-014 section 4 and AC10.
confirm: Tech lead with the front end and the route owner
impact: A changed default or maximum is a contract version change and no business rule changes.

text: The panel states stay READY, STALE_INPUT and DECIDED for SCR-11 and GENERATED, APPROVED and HELD for SCR-18, and loading, temporarily unavailable and session expired are the route's own overlay states and not screen states of this baseline.
why: The legacy screens and the platform route declare two vocabularies and one screen has to present both without a third vocabulary.
read: RWB-E2-014 section 15 with RWB-PLT-N001-CON 15 and AC3.
confirm: Business analyst with the front end and the route owner
impact: The screen's state names and the route's overlay are fixed; a change is a contract version and a screen build step.

text: The notice summary carries noticeId, caseId, noticeType, noticeState, templateId, templateVersion, documentId and generatedAt only; the PDF is served as the document reference by rwb-document at the route, and the addressee role and the masked address are decision-panel fields of rwb-source-data.
why: Legacy AC10 wants the PDF, the addressee role and the masked address on the screen, and the notice answer of rwb-comms carries none of them.
read: RWB-E2-014 AC10 with RWB-P6-E1052-CON AC2, BR8 and 12.1.
confirm: Data steward with the rwb-comms and rwb-document owners
impact: No notice body, addressee or account number crosses the boundary; the screen still shows all three facts from their owners.

text: Every field of the two panels declares a mask flag of NONE, PARTIAL or FULL with a policy key; the postal address is PARTIAL, identifiers and codes are NONE, and the mask itself is applied by the route with the policy of rwb-access.
why: The legacy story names a masked address and no source lists a per-field flag, so the contract has to publish one to be testable.
read: RWB-E2-014 section 4 step 4 with Architecture v5 slide 35, the masking_rule owner P4 and RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC3.
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer with the masking owner
impact: A field without a flag fails the build; if a policy key differs, the contract and the route mapping change and no field is added.

text: The route of the approval screen is registered with a 2 s budget per downstream and the same 1.2 s composition budget as the case screen (0.15 s gateway and session, 0.6 s slowest parallel call, 0.3 s merge).
why: No source states a budget for a screen that composes the approval, the notice and the account facts, and the registration cannot be made without one.
read: RWB-PLT-N001-CON AC2 and AC4 with Architecture v5 slide 10.
confirm: Platform route owner with the service owner
impact: A different budget changes one registration value and one alert threshold; no business rule changes.

text: The service alerts on any 5xx in five minutes, on a route p95 above the registered budget, on a decision record that cannot be written, and on an empty D7.1 queue for 24 hours, with a dashboard showing the error rate, the p95 of the route and the three decisions, the age of the oldest waiting item and the queue size.
why: ADR-023 requires per-service observability and no source names the dashboard, the thresholds or the empty-queue window.
read: ADR-023 with RWB-E2-014 section 2 (measure, 100 percent) and section 3 (1 working day service level).
confirm: Platform observability owner with the service owner
impact: Thresholds are configuration; a review changes rules and not code.
